source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text: Durian (ធូរេន) is a fruit tree that can be grown across a wide range of Cambodia's tropical climate zones, and is especially well suited to the highland soils of the northeast and the lowland soils of the southwest. Farmers today have access to more cultivation technology than in the past, which lets them produce durian more efficiently and get fruit ready for market faster. Skilled growers who master good propagation and orchard techniques can produce fruit reliably and improve the taste and market value of their harvest, but this requires the farmer to keep learning and adapting to the specific soil and climate conditions of their own plot.
